definitions.explanation: A piece of armor carried to protect the body in combat. In modern Japanese, commonly used figuratively to mean something that protects or serves as a defense.
Something used as a protective cover for one's true intentions or actions. Often appears in the phrase 〜を{盾|たて}にする (to use ~ as a shield/excuse).

examples.japanese: {武士|ぶし}は{盾|たて}と{刀|かたな}を{持|も}って{戦|たたか}った。
examples.english: The samurai fought with shields and swords.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{病気|びょうき}を{盾|たて}にして{仕事|しごと}を{休|やす}んだ。
examples.english: He used his illness as an excuse to take time off work.
examples.notes: 〜を盾にする = to use ~ as an excuse/shield

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}を{盾|たて}にして{逃|に}げるのは{卑怯|ひきょう}だ。
examples.english: It's cowardly to escape using a child as a shield.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{盾|たて}を{構|かま}えてデモ{隊|たい}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: The police held up shields and faced the demonstrators.

examples.japanese: {権利|けんり}を{盾|たて}にして{要求|ようきゅう}を{通|とお}す。
examples.english: To push through demands using one's rights as a shield.
examples.notes: Sense 2: using something as a pretext

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{盾|たて}では{弾|たま}は{防|ふせ}げない。
examples.english: A wooden shield can't stop bullets.

examples.japanese: {法律|ほうりつ}を{盾|たて}にして{支払|しはら}いを{拒否|きょひ}した。
examples.english: They refused payment using the law as a shield.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{仕事|しごと}を{盾|たて}にして{誘|さそ}いを{断|ことわ}った。
examples.english: She turned down the invitation using work as an excuse.

examples.japanese: {騎士|きし}は{盾|たて}で{矢|や}を{防|ふせ}いだ。
examples.english: The knight blocked the arrows with his shield.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しさを{盾|たて}にして{会議|かいぎ}を{欠席|けっせき}した。
examples.english: I was absent from the meeting, using being busy as an excuse.

notes:
USAGE: In modern Japanese, the figurative meaning (excuse, pretext) is more common than the literal meaning (physical shield). Japanese samurai historically did not use shields as commonly as Western soldiers since they needed both hands for swords and bows.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{盾|たて}にする (to use as a shield/excuse)
・{盾|たて}になる (to serve as protection)
・{法|ほう}の{盾|たて} (shield of the law)
・{人権|じんけん}を{盾|たて}にする (to hide behind human rights)

RELATED: {矛|ほこ} (spear) - these two words appear together in the famous Chinese story about contradiction ({矛盾|むじゅん}).
